name: toggle-switch
title: Two-node Boolean network (MaBoSS / cmaboss)
question: Driven as a process-bigraph process, does MaBoSS advance a two-node Boolean network and emit bounded, non-degenerate ensemble on-probabilities for both nodes?
hypothesis: Running the A-activated-by-B / B-repressed-by-A network through cmaboss, advancing one coupling interval at a time, yields ensemble on-probabilities that stay in (0,1) and settle near 0.5 for both nodes (the network's limit-cycle signature), with neither node locking to 0 or 1.
objective: Demonstrate end to end that viva_maboss.composites.toggle.maboss_toggle_switch runs the real MaBoSS engine and emits per-interval Boolean states and ensemble on-probabilities, with MaBoSS acting as a pluggable process-bigraph process.
description: The basic-functionality showcase for viva-maboss. A two-node MaBoSS network is advanced interval by interval by the cmaboss backend; each interval re-samples the joint state and emits each node's Boolean state and ensemble on-probability. Over a 30-interval run the last-10-interval mean on-probabilities are A = 0.529, B = 0.520 — both bounded in (0,1), the signature of the network's 4-state cycle.

expected_behavior.name: bounded-marginals
expected_behavior.en: Both nodes' ensemble on-probabilities stay bounded and non-degenerate — time-averaged over the run's tail, each settles inside [0.3, 0.7].
expected_behavior.condition: averaged over the last 10 coupling intervals
expected_behavior.rationale: The A=B / B=!A logic is a 4-state limit cycle (00->01->11->10->...), whose stationary marginals sit near 0.5; a correct stochastic run must keep both nodes bounded away from the 0/1 locks.

behavior_tests.name: bounded-marginals
behavior_tests.description: Tail-averaged on-probability of each node in [0.3, 0.7] (observed A = 0.529, B = 0.520 over the last 10 of 30 intervals; neither node locks to 0 or 1).

findings.name: bounded-cycling-marginals
findings.statement: Over a 30-interval run the two nodes' tail-averaged ensemble on-probabilities are A = 0.529 and B = 0.520, both bounded in (0,1) — the signature of the network's 4-state limit cycle, not bistability.
findings.provenance: Observed in an isolated-venv run of the toggle composite on viva-maboss 0.1.3 / cmaboss 1.0.0b34, 2026-11-27 (reproduced by sims/run.py).

conclusion: PASS. Run as a process-bigraph process, MaBoSS advanced the two-node Boolean network and emitted bounded ensemble on-probabilities (A = 0.529, B = 0.520 tail-averaged), with neither node locking to 0 or 1. MaBoSS behaves as a drop-in process-bigraph Boolean engine — the stochastic layer for multiscale composites.

derived.insight: Over a 30-interval run the two nodes' tail-averaged ensemble on-probabilities are A = 0.529 and B = 0.520, both bounded in (0,1) — the signature of the network's 4-state limit cycle, not bistability.
